subject: Segmentation SLA & control matrix — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenvalleyhealth.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <ciso@greenvalleyhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation SLA & control matrix — follow up

Hi Samantha / Rajiv,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a crisp control matrix for your security and procurement teams.

Recap of the call
- Current preference: leaning toward Private (VPC) deployment for PHI and lineage data; Hosted API was evaluated but flagged due to multi-tenant concerns.
- Primary objectives: demonstrable tenant isolation, customer-managed key control, export/egress controls, and long-term audit retention for compliance.
- Timeline: procurement window Q3; technical review with infra & security teams planned for 4/18.

Clarifying questions (so our control matrix is accurate):
1) Data scope: can you confirm the types of data you will route to Redwood? (e.g., full PHI payloads, hashed identifiers, de-identified text)
2) KMS expectations: do you require HSM-backed CMKs (customer-managed keys) or is cloud KMS with customer control acceptable?
3) Audit logs: minimum retention window required and must-have event types (read, write, admin, key usage)?
4) Network constraints: do you need strictly private egress (no public internet) from the inference hosts?
5) On-prem requirement: is air-gapped on-prem deployment being evaluated or VPC + private control plane is sufficient?

I've attached a first-pass isolation-control-matrix.xlsx with the rows we typically get asked about — please mark which items are must-have vs nice-to-have and I'll update.

Next steps
- If you can answer Q1–Q5 by EOD Friday (4/6), we'll produce an updated control matrix and an execution timeline for review.
- We'll also propose an example SLA (latency/cost/capacity) for Private capacity vs Dedicated reserved pool.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity here.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
redwoodinference.com

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenvalleyhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kapoor <ciso@greenvalleyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation SLA & control matrix — follow up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers below so you can proceed with the control matrix:

1) Data scope: primary payloads will include full clinical notes (PHI), limited patient identifiers in metadata, and tokenized insurance IDs.
2) KMS expectations: must be customer-managed. We prefer HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3 or equivalent), but we can accept cloud KMS if it is customer-managed with strong separation.
3) Audit logs: retention target is 7 years. Must include key usage events, admin role changes, data access (read) and inference request hashes (for provenance).
4) Network: private egress only. No public internet from inference hosts; all outbound should be via our VPC endpoints.
5) On-prem: not evaluating fully air-gapped on-prem at this stage; VPC with private control plane + optional dedicated racks is preferred.

One more ask from Rajiv (cc'd): can you map how Redwood handles key escrow / access for disaster recovery and what proofs we can get for key separation?

We'll fill the matrix and flag must-haves by Friday.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director, Product & Privacy | GreenValley Health
samantha@greenvalleyhealth.com

Can you please: 
- Confirm which of the following we can represent as "supported today" vs "roadmap/engineering effort": HSM CMKs (customer-managed), customer KMS key rotation windows, audit export formats (syslog/CloudWatch/ELK), 7-year retention options, private-only host egress, and proof artifacts for key separation (attestation / architecture diagrams).

Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@greenvalleyhealth.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <ciso@greenvalleyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Apr 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Segmentation SLA & control matrix — follow up

Marissa — thanks for the heads up and Samantha / Rajiv for the quick answers. Responses below (high level) — I'll own the artifact delivery.

- HSM CMKs (customer-managed): Supported via our Private deployment using customer KMS integration. We can integrate with customer-managed HSM-backed keys in AWS KMS (CloudHSM) or Azure Dedicated HSM through the Private control plane. We'll surface a one-page KMS integration guide. (Status: supported today in Private; note: Hosted does not support customer HSM CMKs.)

- Key rotation / separation: Customer may rotate keys on their schedule; Redwood never stores plaintext keys. We support key rotation without re-encrypting stored model artifacts (we keep metadata references). We'll document rotation workflows and recommended rotation windows. (Status: supported; doc required.)

- Audit logs & retention: We can stream structured audit events to your log collector (syslog / customer CloudWatch / Event Hubs). Native retention on our side is 90 days; for 7-year retention we recommend streaming to your archive (S3 Glacier / customer archival). We'll provide a sample event schema and retention playbook. (Status: supported via log export; architecture note included.)

- Private-only egress: Private deployment can be configured with no public egress; all outbound traffic routable through customer VPC endpoints / NAT configured by customer. We'll include a network diagram and validation checklist. (Status: supported.)

- Key escrow / DR: For DR we support an optional escrow arrangement where encrypted key metadata is stored with customer-owned KMS references and Redwood can produce an attestation around operational access controls. We will not have escrowed plaintext keys. We'll include a short FAQ on escrow options and the attestations we can provide (eg. signed architecture diagram, runbook excerpts). (Status: supported with attestations; legal review needed for escrow contract language.)

Delivery plan
- I will produce: (1) one-page control map (matches your matrix rows to evidence items), (2) KMS integration guide (1-2 pages), (3) network diagram + validation checklist, (4) sample audit event schema and suggested retention pattern.
- Target delivery: 2028-04-10 for draft artifacts; final set by 2028-04-15 so Marissa can circulate to GVH by 4/18.

Action items for Marissa
- Please confirm whether GVH prefers AWS or Azure for the initial PoC (this affects our example playbook).
- I'll need temporary access to the matrix you attached (Drive link) — I used the placeholder folder in the related_links above.

Thanks — I'll follow up with drafts.

Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
